lines.text: Ten goats eat a field in twenty days. Fifteen need only ten!
lines.caption: Ten goats eat a field in twenty days. Fifteen need only ten!

lines.text: New grass grows steadily. Ten goats take twenty days, fifteen take ten.
lines.caption: New grass grows steadily. Ten goats take twenty days, fifteen take ten.

lines.text: How many days for twenty-five goats?
lines.caption: How many days for twenty-five goats?

lines.text: In goat-days, ten times twenty is two hundred. Fifteen times ten is one hundred fifty.
lines.caption: In goat-days, ten times twenty is two hundred. Fifteen times ten is one hundred fifty.

lines.text: Fifty less: ten fewer days of growth. So grass grows five goat-days a day.
lines.caption: Fifty less: ten fewer days of growth. So grass grows five goat-days a day.

lines.text: Twenty days of growth is one hundred. That leaves a starting pile of one hundred.
lines.caption: Twenty days of growth is one hundred. That leaves a starting pile of one hundred.

lines.text: Twenty-five goats: five keep up with the growth. Twenty eat the pile.
lines.caption: Twenty-five goats: five keep up with the growth. Twenty eat the pile.

lines.text: One hundred over twenty is five days!
lines.caption: One hundred over twenty is five days!

lines.text: Not four. That forgets the growing grass!
lines.caption: Not four. That forgets the growing grass!

lines.text: Why does that work? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why does that work? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
